message.content:
Finding the “best” sushi spot in Los Angeles can feel like a culinary quest—there are dozens of places that pull off everything from classic nigiri to avant‑garde rolls. Below is a quick‑look guide to some of the most celebrated sushi restaurants in the city, grouped by what makes them stand out. Pick the one that matches your vibe, budget, and craving!

| Restaurant | Why It’s Notable | Typical Price Range | Highlights |
|------------|-----------------|---------------------|------------|
| **Sushi Gen** (Mid-Wilshire) | 3‑star Michelin (2022) – the only Michelin‑starred sushi in LA. | $70–$120 per person | Omakase, fresh toro, impeccable service |
| **Sushi Park** (West Hollywood) | Known for its “sushi bar” concept and high‑quality fish. | $50–$90 per person | Omakase, seasonal sashimi, great for groups |
| **Sushi Roku** (Multiple locations) | Trendy, modern take on sushi with a global twist. | $40–$80 per person | Signature rolls, creative cocktails |
| **Kazu** (Beverly Hills) | Intimate, chef‑driven experience with a focus on seasonal ingredients. | $60–$100 per person | Omakase, personalized tasting menu |
| **Sushi Tetsu** (West Hollywood) | Small, no‑frills spot that delivers pure, traditional sushi. | $30–$60 per person | Classic nigiri, friendly staff |
| **Sushi Kappo** (Beverly Hills) | Combines kaiseki and sushi in a refined setting. | $80–$150 per person | Multi‑course kaiseki, sushi, sake pairing |
| **Sushi Neko** (West Hollywood) | Known for its “sushi bar” and creative rolls. | $35–$70 per person | Unique roll combinations, lively atmosphere |
| **Sushi Saito** (West Hollywood) | A hidden gem with a focus on precision and quality. | $50–$90 per person | Omakase, meticulous plating |
| **Sushi Tatsu** (West Hollywood) | A small, family‑run spot that offers a relaxed vibe. | $25–$55 per person | Fresh fish, friendly service |
| **Sushi Ota** (West Hollywood) | A long‑standing favorite for its authentic Japanese feel. | $30–$60 per person | Traditional sushi, great value |

### How to Choose

| Factor | What to Look For |
|--------|------------------|
| **Budget** | Omakase at Sushi Gen is pricey; Sushi Tatsu is more affordable. |
| **Atmosphere** | Intimate & formal (Sushi Gen, Kazu) vs. casual & lively (Sushi Tatsu, Sushi Neko). |
| **Specialty** | Traditional nigiri (Sushi Tetsu), creative rolls (Sushi Roku), kaiseki (Sushi Kappo). |
| **Location** | Downtown (Sushi Gen), West Hollywood (most others), Beverly Hills (Kazu, Sushi Kappo). |
| **Reservations** | High‑end spots (Sushi Gen, Kazu) require booking months in advance. |

### Quick Tips

1. **Reserve Early** – Especially for Michelin‑starred or popular spots.  
2. **Ask About Omakase** – Many places offer a chef‑selected tasting menu that showcases the freshest fish of the day.  
3. **Check the Fish Menu** – Freshness is key; a good sushi spot will have a daily fish menu posted.  
4. **Try the Sake** – Pairing sushi with a well‑chosen sake can elevate the experience.  

### Bottom Line

If you’re after the pinnacle of sushi craftsmanship, **Sushi Gen** is the place to go. For a more relaxed yet still high‑quality experience, **Sushi Park** or **Sushi Tetsu** are excellent choices. If you want something trendy and creative, **Sushi Roku** or **Sushi Neko** will satisfy.  

Enjoy your sushi adventure in LA! 🍣
